Alirocumab versus placebo: percent change in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24

In adults treated for hypercholesterolaemia, how much does alirocumab change calculated LDL cholesterol from baseline to week 24 compared with placebo?

Percent change from baseline in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24

Percent change from baseline in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24

Pooled result

MD -54.82 (-60.23 to -49.42), 95% interval

Percent change from baseline in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24. random, estimator DerSimonian-Laird, k = 8.

τ² 50.04 · I² 88% · Q 58.42 on 7 df

Favours: the intervention (lower is better)

high

How to read this: Between-trial variation is high: I-squared is 88.0 per cent and tau-squared 50.04. The trials differ in background statin therapy, in population, and in dose regimen, so the pooled figure summarises a range of settings rather than estimating one common effect. Heterogeneity was already high at k=6 (I-squared 87.9) and the recovery did not create it.

Prediction interval -72.77 to -36.87

THIS IS THE NUMBER TO QUOTE, and it is not the headline. The confidence interval -60.2 to -49.4 is about where the AVERAGE lies. The prediction interval -72.8 to -36.9 is about where the effect in a NEW trial of this drug would lie, and it is over three times wider. The eight trials range from -39.1 to -64.1 with tight intervals of their own, so the spread is real and not sampling noise: dose regimen differs, as do population and background statin therapy. A single number for 'how much does alirocumab lower LDL' conceals a 25-point range.

About this estimator: INHERITED AND OPEN, NOT ENDORSED. This object declares DerSimonian-Laird, which is biased for k<10. That was already questionable at k=6 and remains so at k=8. REML on the same eight trials gives -54.72 (-60.62 to -48.82) with tau2 61.44 and I-squared 90.0, and a prediction interval of -71.18 to -38.26. It is reported BESIDE the DL figure rather than substituted for it, because changing the estimator and the trial set in one step would make neither change attributable. A reader should treat the estimator choice as open.

What other estimators give on the same values

Estimatorτ²I²Pooled (95%)
DerSimonian-Laird (as displayed)50.0488%-54.82 (-60.23 to -49.42)
REML61.4490%-54.72 (-60.62 to -48.82)
REML with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman
t_7 = 2.3646, not a normal quantile		61.4490%-54.72 (-62.06 to -47.38)

The point estimate barely moves -- 54.8 against 54.7 percent -- and no reading of the direction or the magnitude changes. THE INTERVAL MOVES: 10.8 points wide under DerSimonian-Laird, 11.8 under REML, 14.7 under REML with Hartung-Knapp. A reader who wants the most conservative statement of what eight trials establish should take the last of those.

I-SQUARED SITS EXACTLY ON THE THRESHOLD, AND WHICH SIDE DEPENDS ON THE DEFINITION AS WELL AS THE ESTIMATOR. 88.0 per cent under DerSimonian-Laird and 90.0 under REML on metafor's definition; 88.0 under BOTH on Higgins's. This project's poolability screen treats 90 per cent as the point at which an average conceals more than it conveys, so at k=8 the verdict on whether these eight trials should be averaged at all lands ON the line rather than clearly either side of it. At k=6 the REML figure was 91.6 and clearly across. THE RECOVERY MOVED THIS TOWARD POOLABILITY, which is the opposite direction from the one that would flatter a decision already taken, and is stated for that reason.

Comparison with published syntheses

Eight trials, one endpoint, and every value posted by the registry -- so the trial-by-trial check here is complete in a way it cannot be where trials post no results. It is also the topic where the error found is OURS, and it is in the table below with the same weight as anything found in the literature.

12 checks were applied and 8 came back clean, 1 found an error, 1 found something absent and 2 could not be settled at the layer available. The denominator is stated because a list of only the failures is not a finding, it is a selection.

Confirmations are listed in the same table, in the same detail, as errors. Across the cardiology topics reconciled so far the published literature has been implicated in none of them: where a defect existed it was ours. A comparison with room only for their errors could not have found that out.

checked and clean		All six registry records give the outcome as 'Percent Change From Baseline in Calculated LDL-C at Week 24' on the intention-to-treat analysis. The only differences are orthographic -- one record writes 'Intent--to--Treat' with doubled hyphens, another closes the bracket after 'ITT Analysis' rather than before it. Compared as whole normalised fields, which is the rule this repository once broke inside its own auditor by testing a fragment.
Quoted: “Percent Change From Baseline in Calculated LDL-C at Week 24 - Intent-to-Treat (ITT) Analysis” — ClinicalTrials.gov, all six records, outcome measure title
Whether any of the six is actually an ACTIVE-comparator trial
comparator-is-placebo-on-all-six		CONFIRMED
checked and clean		None is. All six registry records type the control arm PLACEBO_COMPARATOR. This was checked rather than assumed because the ODYSSEY programme contains sibling trials with different comparators, and a published review states it independently: 'ODYSSEY COMBO I and ODYSSEY COMBO II studies demonstrated significant superiority of alirocumab ... in comparison to placebo and ezetimibe, respectively'. NCT01644175 is COMBO I, the placebo-controlled one, and COMBO II is not in this set. A pool silently mixing a placebo contrast with an ezetimibe contrast would have been an average over two different questions.
Quoted: “ODYSSEY COMBO I and ODYSSEY COMBO II studies demonstrated significant superiority of alirocumab on LDL-cholesterol lowering in comparison to placebo and ezetimibe, respectively” — PMID 29299849, abstract; and the armGroups type on all six records
The between-study variance estimator used for the headline
our-estimator-breaks-our-own-rule		ERROR
a defect, in the source named		THIS ONE IS OURS. The pool is DerSimonian-Laird at k=8, and this project's own statistical rules say not to use DerSimonian-Laird below about ten studies because it underestimates the between-trial variance and narrows the interval. Recomputed on exactly these six values: REML gives tau-squared 71.2 against 47.4, and I-squared 91.6 per cent against 87.9. THE VERDICT ON WHETHER THESE TRIALS SHOULD BE AVERAGED AT ALL TURNS ON THAT, because this project's own poolability screen treats 90 per cent as the point where an average conceals more than it conveys -- so the estimator that the rules advise against is the one that keeps the pool on the acceptable side of the threshold. The headline is NOT re-estimated in this pass: the same estimator is used across this corpus including the flagship, and changing one page alone would make it inconsistent with its neighbours without fixing anything. It is recorded in the open, with the alternatives printed beside it, rather than quietly left or quietly changed.
this object, results.ldlc_pct_change_wk24.estimator and estimator_sensitivity
Whether any published synthesis pools these eight trials on this endpoint
no-synthesis-reports-this-estimand		ABSENT
the thing checked for is not there		None located. The closest are a familial-hypercholesterolaemia pool of seven trials across BOTH PCSK9 antibodies, weighted mean difference -49.14% (-55.81 to -42.47), and a twelve-trial alirocumab review reporting 'over 50%' with no interval. Both overlap our -54.82% and neither answers the same question. So this pooled value cannot be checked against an external number, which is a statement about the literature rather than a claim of novelty.
Quoted: “PCSK9-mAbs reduced the LDL-C level by the greatest margin, WMD -49.14%, 95% CI: -55.81 to -42.47%, on FH versus control groups” — PMID 34754882, abstract
A network meta-analysis reporting a much larger reduction
network-estimates-further-from-zero		UNRESOLVED
could not be settled at the layer available		It reports alirocumab-versus-placebo relative effects of -71.45 (-91.16 to -50.44), -74.32 (-90.40 to -58.63) and -77.28 (-92.21 to -61.90) by dose strategy -- all further from zero than our -54.82, and all with intervals around forty points wide. It cannot be settled from the abstract whether those are percent changes on the same basis, and an interval that wide is compatible with a wide range of truths. Recorded for a reader rather than asserted as a discrepancy in either direction.
Quoted: “alirocumab could significantly reduce LDL-c levels, compared with placebo (relative effect 95 % CI: -71.45 [-91.16, -50.44], -74.32 [-90.40, -58.63] and -77.28 [-92.21, -61.90])” — PMID 30782243, abstract
Whether the 97 syntheses that name no trial included ours
what-the-abstract-layer-cannot-settle		UNRESOLVED
could not be settled at the layer available		97 of 101 records name none of our eight trials in the abstract and two carry no indexed abstract. Alirocumab LDL-lowering is a crowded literature and many of those certainly do include these trials; which ones, and on what endpoint, cannot be decided from an abstract.

The syntheses reconciled against

Table 12. The syntheses reconciled against
34754882A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Therapeutic Efficacy and Safety of Alirocumab and Evolocumab on Familial Hypercholesterolemia. Biomed Res Int 2022.
It pools BOTH drugs and restricts to familial hypercholesterolaemia; we pool one drug across a mixed population. Its weighted mean difference -49.14% (-55.81 to -42.47) is a different set of trials answering a narrower question, and it overlaps ours.
30782243Efficacy and safety of different doses of alirocumab in reducing low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels: a network meta-analysis. Pharmazie 2019.
A NETWORK estimate over sixteen studies rather than a direct pool over six, and its intervals are about forty points wide. Its alirocumab-versus-placebo relative effects run from -71 to -77, further from zero than our -54.8, and the abstract does not state the unit or the model well enough to say why.
31463238Safety and efficacy of alirocumab: A meta analysis of 12 randomized controlled trials. J Family Med Prim Care 2019.
It reports 'over 50%' LDL-C reduction without a pooled interval in its abstract, so it supplies a direction and a rough magnitude and no number to reconcile against.
29299849Lipid Management in Chronic Kidney Disease: Systematic Review of PCSK9 Targeting. Drugs 2019.
It reports no pooled estimate, but it is the record that independently confirms which ODYSSEY COMBO trial used which comparator -- see the comparator check.

Where the numbers differ, and why

Table 13. Where the numbers differ, and why
This reviewMean difference -54.82 percent (-60.23 to -49.42) in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24, k=8, random effects, DerSimonian-Laird. PREDICTION INTERVAL -72.8 to -36.9, which is the number to quote.
The published synthesis-49.14% (-55.81 to -42.47) over seven familial-hypercholesterolaemia trials of both PCSK9 antibodies; 'over 50%' over twelve alirocumab trials; -71 to -77 by dose in a sixteen-study network analysis.
Why they differDifferent eligible sets and different questions -- one drug or two, one population or several, direct pool or network. Nothing here shows either side in error on the numbers. THE SUBSTANTIVE POINT IS NOT THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN REVIEWS, IT IS THE SPREAD WITHIN OURS: eight trials running from -39.1 to -64.1, each with a tight interval of its own, I-squared near 90 per cent. A single number for 'how much does alirocumab lower LDL' conceals a twenty-five point range, and the prediction interval is the only honest summary of it.

How they were identified: PubMed E-utilities; query, counts and a per-record decision in ssot/alirocumab-lipid/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json. 101 records matched and all 101 were read at abstract level.
